title: Form 1040 instructions (2025), Tax Table example: joint, taxable income $25,300: tax $2,562

source.where: Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), page 68, the Tax Table example

expectedFailure.reason: Wages 56,800 less the 2025 joint standard deduction (31,500, Publication 17 (2025)) are 25,300 taxable, which the estimate now gets right (T4 prices each year with its own law); the estimate uses the bracket formula, 2,385 + 12% x 1,450 = 2,559, where the Tax Table uses the middle of each $50 band (T23): 2025 brackets at 25,325 give 2,385 + 12% x 1,475 = 2,562.

note: The IRS example gives the tax from the table, 2,562; 2025 joint brackets are 10% to 23,850 and 12% above (Rev. Proc. 2024-40), so the table's middle of the band, 25,325, gives 2,385 + 177 = 2,562.

title: Publication 596 (2025), page 5: single, one qualifying child, AGI $53,000: no earned income credit

source.where: Publication 596 (2025), page 5, Example: AGI is more than limit ($50,434 for one child)

note: AGI 53,000 is over the 2025 limit 50,434. It also gives 0 under the estimate's 2026 table; it is a year-2025 case that will be checked on 2025 law once the estimator reads the year (T4).

title: Publication 501 (2025), Example 1: 16-year-old dependent, wages $150, interest $780: standard deduction $1,350

source.where: Publication 501 (2025), Standard Deduction for Dependents, Example 1

expectedFailure.reason: The estimate gives a dependent the full standard deduction (audit 4.5.7); T5 adds the limit.

note: Earned income 150 + 450 = 600; the larger of 600 and 1,350 is 1,350, under the regular 15,750.

title: Publication 501 (2025), Example 3: blind 18-year-old dependent, wages $2,900, interest $1,300: standard deduction $5,350

source.where: Publication 501 (2025), Standard Deduction for Dependents, Example 3

expectedFailure.reason: The estimate gives a dependent the full standard deduction and ignores blindness (audit 4.5.2, 4.5.7); T5 adds both.

note: 2,900 + 450 = 3,350, then 2,000 more for an unmarried blind person: 5,350.
